reading.body:
A mistagged OpenStreetMap point for a software office is not a data center, and it should not be counted in Arizona's AI infrastructure.

The entry carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no published specifications. Its coordinates resolve to a different current tenant, Safe T Professionals LLC, at 25 South Arizona Place in Chandler. Emailage was a fraud-prevention and email-risk-scoring company that ran on cloud and outsourced infrastructure, acquired by LexisNexis Risk Solutions. Nothing in the record ties this address to servers or hosting.

The pattern matters because facility counts are only as good as their tagging. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, of which only 4 publish capacity figures, totaling 512 MW. A single mistagged software office does not move that total, but it shows how a former company address can enter a dataset as infrastructure and stay there. For AI specifically, the binding constraint is power and buildings, and this row describes neither.

What the data does not tell the reader is how many other entries in the 56 share this problem. It also does not establish when the tenant changed or why the point was tagged as a data center. The record is exhausted, not resolved.
